chunks: Has not the account of those before them come to them, -- of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud, of Abraham and Midian, and all the habitations that were destroyed? Their apostles had come to them with clear proofs; and God did not surely wrong them, they wronged themselves.

key_terms.الْمُؤْتَفِكَاتِ: The destroyed cities (specifically Sodom and Gomorrah)

ai.seo_question: Who are the historical communities mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah as examples of divine justice?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse serves as a rhetorical warning to the Quraysh, linking their current rejection of Prophet Muhammad to the fate of earlier nations like 'Ad and Thamud who were destroyed despite receiving clear proofs (bayyinat). It highlights the principle of 'self-injustice' (dhulm al-nafs), where divine punishment is a consequence of internal moral corruption rather than arbitrary divine caprice. The mention of 'the Overthrown Cities' (Al-Mu'tafikat) specifically alludes to Sodom and Gomorrah, reinforcing the theme of divine retribution for communal sin.
